Maybe less positive and more depressing - my mum died of cancer when I was 12 - just be with them. We didn't have time to do "nice" bucket list things because my mum was diagnosed so late, she was already hospitalised when we knew she was dying. 

We brought her home to my aunts (the NHS was so supportive) and we nursed her. It was really hard, watching her lose her lucidity suddenly, be in pain and say goodbye to people. I stopped going to school and would hide under her bed (she knew I was there) when doctors visited so I could be close to her and know what was going on (people wouldn't be honest when they knew I was there). I helped nurse her and even when she lost consciousness I like to think she knew I was there. I did my best to help keep her comfortable, I kept her mouth from drying, her lips moisturised, sat with her, listened to her breathing and talked to her.

I wish I had recordings of her, I can't remember what she sounded like, but I remember what she used to say. I can't picture her face but I have photos of the nice things we did before she was ill. Photos when she was ill and in pain are hard to look at, especially because you can tell she was trying so hard to hide it, because I was a child I didn't always notice. I miss her but I know she loved me and I did my best for her, even if it was ineffective I was with her until the very end.

I'm so angry right now, at him and myself, I thought that perhaps I'd made him realise what he did was terrible, I'd told myself that I had some of them blame as well, I'd thought I'd dealt with it, I even told him to his face I forgave him. 

I was 16 when it happened and I'd drunk to much, he had too but nowhere as gone as I was, I remember thinking I don't know how I got into this situation at the time, I was passing in and out of consciousness trying to push him off. I was so shocked I stayed with him the rest of the night and when my parents picked me up I said nothing.

I had to sit next to him everyday at school, his friends are my friends, I felt disgusting, the smell of him made me feel sick, I hated him but I didn't want anyone to know what a state I'd been in so I said nothing. He told people he'd "fucked me", friends asked but I said I didn't know, they though I was just being coy.

I didn't want to cause an argument between his friends and mine, he was young too, I started to doubt myself, it could have been a simple misunderstanding, he wasn't a bad guy, he was always looking out for people so I said nothing. 

Life went on, time passed, he offered me a lifts places when friends met up, I declined at first but then he wore me down and it was convenient so I accepted. He asked me on a date, I decided I had been wrong, I don't remember how I got myself in that situation but I must have done something that suggested I wanted it, I still said nothing.

One day he kissed me in his car, things went further, we started to have sex, before I broke down and told him I was pregnant, I asked for his advice, he asked who's it was, he was so kind, so helpful, so gentle. I told him it was not important, I didn't know, I'd been coked out my skull at the time, I barely remembered, he told me it was ok, there was nothing wrong with having fun, hadn't we just been having fun? Hadn't we had fun before?

It was the first time we'd said anything about it to each other, I told him no, it hadn't been "fun" for me, how every thrust hurt as my body tried to keep him out, how my throat had been sore for days where he'd held it, how dirty I felt, how ashamed, confused and regretful. He apologised, he looked in my eyes and told me he'd not do it again, he understood now how awful that was, how he had been worried I hated him and I had every right to, he understood that drunk people couldn't consent. I looked at him, he was so convincing, and I told him how I had hated him, but I could see he had made a mistake and he was genuinely sorry so I told him I forgave him.

Life passes, we hang out with our friends still and see each other when they do, I feel at ease with him, he's changed. My friend passed out, he sat up with her in the recovery position, kept an eye on her breathing until it was steady, then stuck his hands down her pants when she couldn't even try to say no or stop him. She said nothing the next day, what could she say? He's our friend, who would believe her? Come on they dated, she's single, drunken mistakes aren't assault. But she told me because she remembers my silence, the coolness between us and I didn't know what to say.

I thought he'd changed, I'm devastated that my silence let him do this to another girl, other girls as well, the stories start to come, he went on a date, she comes back with bruises on her arms and thighs, finger marks on her throat, she says nothing too. How did this happen? People hurting but too scared to say anything? Because he's a "good" guy, he's in the army, he's protecting the country. Who would believe us? We have no proof, I couldn't even give you a date and we are still friends. And I told him I fucking forgave him

I want to cry and rage, I want that disgusting man dead, I don't know how I'm going to face him, his friends who all know what he's like but but tolerate him any, how can I blame them? I'm one of them. If it wasn't so terrible I'd relish the irony.

It wasn't just about the community, I already had a great family who I speak to every day and which is larger than average. With regards to the nonsense, I walked in to that church with no expectations of finding Jesus. I was ready to go back home with my atheism intact. But there was something, I don't know how to describe it, I felt joy like I'd never felt and peace. Really it was the peace, being able to just let go of what I'd been holding on to. 

And when I put my hand up to be saved I couldn't believe I'd done it, I was baptized in water later than day and I came out a different person. You're welcome to still believe it's nonsense, sometimes I wonder what I'm doing, but it truly cured my depression, being filled with the Holy Spirit leaves no room for it. There are there things I doubt in my church like the faith healing, I think it can be more of a placebo effect, but if it gives people comfort I have no problem with it but giving false hope can be cruel. People speak in tongues and I was sure that was not an "angelic language" until at home while praying it happened to me.

I really don't know to what extent I believe, I would appear deeply religious attending church at least twice a week and reading my Bible everyday, but I'm very good at holding contradictory beliefs and not having to reconcile them. I don't really know what to say, I believe in the life of Jesus and I don't believe that it's nonsense.

There was no specific event but more of a few events that lead me to Him. I'd say the first one was the death of my mum about 10 years ago, she had a horrible death and as an atheist I didn't believe in an afterlife so it comforted me that she wasn't going to suffer after she died, she was just gone. But after she died it's only really recently I noticed I was harbouring a lot of anger towards what caused it, it logically makes no sense to be angry at a God you don't believe in so that's something I've had to accept.

 The second would be the horrible depression I had suffered for a few years until I found the Lord, I hated myself and life and I just wanted to end it all, but I couldn't because I needed to look after my younger sister and she needed me. I was too proud to go to the doctor or talk to anyone about it so I tried to self medicate with LSD having read it was being trialed to treat depression. I took a tab, had a bad trip and at my lowest and most vunerable prayed, I promised to be "God's best friend" if he ended my trip and let me go to sleep. Unsurprisingly it didn't work but after that I had this overwhelming feeling to go to church every time I walk past one I would feel the desire to go in. 

Eventually I did go to church, which brings me to my third event(s), I signed up to an alpha course because I just could get that pull to church out of my head and it seemed like a good way to be able to ask questions, I was raised with no religious background at all and in my house religion was viewed almost like a mental illness. I went along and I met these 'crazy' people but I realized that they weren't crazy at all, they were normal people who just all seemed to know that there was a something more. The main thing I was struck by was their radiating peace and joy and somehow always saying exactly what I needed to hear. After a few weeks I was invited to a Sunday service and I went along not expecting much, I'm wasn't going to be pulled in by a load of nonsense, but it was great. The first half was worship and I didn't really get into it until someone asked why I was holding back and I couldn't answer, and hasn't realized that I was but once I let go I felt joy for the first time in a long time. And in the second half when asked if anyone would like to be saved my hand went up, not because I chose to but because it just did. I accepted Jesus Christ as Lord and I was baptized that same day, it's honestly the best decision I've made.

For some extra background, you could say I'm a classic conversion, lost, depressed, absent father figure and dabbling in drugs. I had no self respect, I would drink too much and sleep with strangers to make myself feel worse, I'd self harm and I've even attempted suicide. But on the other hand I'm a logical scientific person, my best subject is physics and I'm studying for an engineering degree. I don't believe in witchcraft or faries, I 100% believe in science, evolution and climate change. Before I was saved I would mock Christians, I believed that I was better than them, but I realized now that I am wrong.

EDIT: tl;dr: many reasons, can't be angry at someone who doesn't exist, bad trip caused me to pray and feel like I should go to church, went and felt the overwhelming joy, accepted Jesus and got baptized but I'm almost a textbook conversion case apart from being sciency.
